response.markdown_report:
The best early-stage experiment remains **shared-weight, context-gated dilation inside corrected NextItNet**, revised to use nonsaturated initialization and a matched static-gate control. Preserve one jointly trained network per category. No execution or improvement is claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Different dilations expose different temporal offsets; usefulness may depend on the prefix. (2) Sharing corresponding branch parameters limits additional capacity, but similar branch outputs can weaken gate learning. (3) Gates control transformations of contextualized states; short dilation does not guarantee removal of older information.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Selective Kernel Networks provide a closer multiscale-selection precedent than WaveNet or Highway Networks, but require causal adaptation. (2) SkipRec and AdaMCT weaken broad novelty claims about contextual computation selection; neither establishes this shared-kernel mechanism. (3) FADC and HGNCDSR motivate adaptive scale and interest processing without proving recommendation gains or forgetting. R²NS supports a separate sampling direction.

The framework separates **accessible evidence** (full prefixes versus explicit windows), **transformation selection** (fixed versus adaptive dilation), and **candidate discrimination** (inherited loss versus additional negatives). These organize three directions without conflating their mechanisms.

| Atomic idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Shared-weight dilation gate | 3 | 6 | 6 | 5 | 6 |
| Strict recent-ten windows | 2 | 6 | 6 | 4 | 6 |
| Uniform multi-negative CE | 3 | 6 | 4 | 7 | 4 |

Positive/negative assessments, respectively: **gate**—originality: specific shared-kernel synthesis/established adaptive selection; potential: controlled temporal processing/uncertain generalization; user alignment: targets recent-purpose displacement/cannot infer unmet need; model alignment: tests contextual confusion/no causal diagnosis; difficulty: few parameters/dual forwards, stochastic controls and predictor parity. **Windows**—clear intervention/familiar truncation; useful control/lost persistent interests; excludes distant evidence/recent evidence can mislead; tests interference/weak attribution; reused backbone/repeated computation. **CE**—focused discrimination/standard objective; optimization control/sampled gains may not transfer; challenges weak alternatives/no recency mechanism; targets margins/training overfit; unchanged inference/careful sampling.

**Selected mechanism.** Blend complete original- and unit-dilation residual updates using one causal scalar gate per position and block. Initialize logits at zero; compare against a learned context-independent gate initialized identically. This replaces the earlier −4 bias, which approximately preserves the original path but suppresses gate gradients. Retain inherited training settings.

The behavioral targets remain broad relevance displacing specific recent-purpose matches and isolated older interactions becoming persistent preferences. Neither improvement nor compatibility reasoning follows from the mechanism alone. The quantitative target remains Industrial_and_Scientific’s 8.04% negative-outranking rate and 0.2551 tenth-percentile margin. Preserve fixed diagnostic negatives; cosine-derived scores near 0.5 do not establish dimensional collapse.

Prioritize the corrected baseline, static gate and contextual gate; additional fixed-mixture or initialization controls require remaining budget. Measure gate gradients, saturation, context variation and branch differences. Select through unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, and inspect the prescribed twenty users separately. Sampled metrics cannot establish full-catalog improvements [Krichene and Rendle].

idea.description: Within each corrected NextItNet residual block, evaluate its complete residual transformation at the inherited dilations and at unit dilation using corresponding shared parameters. A causal scalar gate at each position interpolates these transformations before adding the unchanged identity shortcut. Initialize gate logits at zero and compare against a context-independent scalar gate initialized to the same mixture. Train exactly one network and retain one selected checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: At 10% research progress, a bounded architectural experiment remains appropriate, provided its optimization and attribution problems are addressed before adding objectives, metadata processing or mining. The two explicit user-facing targets are broadly related items displacing specific recent-purpose matches and isolated older interactions being extended into persistent preferences. Adaptive dilation may help distinguish these contexts, but neither branch directly identifies current intent, compatibility, replacement need or satisfied demand. The model-facing target is the current Industrial_and_Scientific diagnosis: 8.04% sampled negatives outrank positives, with a tenth-percentile margin of 0.2551. Earlier inspiration metrics belong to different runs and must not replace these measurements. Uniform multi-negative CE remains a practical alternative if dual-branch training is unaffordable; strict windows remain the clearer intervention when the research question concerns exclusion of distant raw inputs. The reported inspiration scores do not establish causal superiority of any mechanism.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integration boundary: this remains an integration specification and pseudocode, not a standalone replacement train.py. The prompt does not contain the corrected baseline source. Preserve its actual backbone, family-specific sampler, optimizer, loss, initialization of shared parameters, normalization, dropout and checkpoint schedule rather than inventing missing details. Record these inherited settings and the complete dilation schedule before execution. The official TensorFlow NextItNet block is an architectural reference, not permission to overwrite a different supplied corrected implementation.

Branch construction: expose each supplied block's complete residual branch without its shortcut. Evaluate it twice using the same corresponding learned convolution weights, biases and tokenwise normalization parameters: once at every inherited temporal dilation and once with each temporal dilation replaced by one. Sharing is across the two evaluations of each corresponding operation; do not tie the first convolution to the second convolution within a block. Preserve kernels, nonlinearities, operation order and inherited output processing. The official two-convolution block uses dilations d and 2d; its unit-dilation counterpart therefore uses 1 and 1. Record the actual supplied schedule instead of assuming it matches the reference.

Implement dilation as an explicit functional argument, without mutating module attributes between forwards. For B x C x L input, kernel size k, stride one and dilation d, use F.conv1d(F.pad(x, ((k-1)*d, 0)), weight, bias, dilation=d, padding=0). Adapt this expression only as required by the supplied convolution representation. LayerNorm(C) operates over channels independently at each timestep, ordinarily after transposing to B x L x C. Normalization over time can introduce future dependence and must not be introduced. If the supplied implementation has incompatible cross-example or temporal normalization, identify the incompatibility rather than silently changing the experiment.

Gate definition: let h be the block input and r_t the causal, padding-masked mean of the original item embeddings at positions max(0,t-4) through t, dividing by the number of nonpadding entries clamped to at least one. The summary uses the original item embeddings rather than deeply contextualized states. For each nonredundant block, alpha_t=sigmoid(Linear(concat(h_t,r_t))), with one output channel and one separately learned projection per block. Compute update=(1-alpha)*original_update+alpha*short_update, then add the inherited shortcut and restore padding zeros. Do not gate the shortcut or combine independent prediction scores.

Initialization revision: initialize contextual gate weights and biases to zero, giving alpha=0.5. The earlier weight-zero, bias-minus-four proposal gave alpha approximately 0.018 and sigmoid derivative approximately 0.01766, compared with 0.25 at zero. Its near-original initialization and saturation are competing considerations; Highway Networks' identity-propagation rationale does not establish that a strong bias helps choose between two transformed branches. The revised initialization does not reproduce baseline outputs: it starts from equal mixing. For this orientation, the gate-logit derivative is alpha*(1-alpha)*(short_update-original_update). Similar branch outputs and saturated logits independently weaken the learning signal. Zero projection weights receive gradients but initially block gate-mediated gradients into h and r; ordinary backbone paths still train their inputs. Bias-minus-four may be a separately declared initialization ablation if budget permits, not an undisclosed default or a promised improvement.

Padding: mask item embeddings initially and restore zero padded states before every temporal convolution. Biased convolutions and affine normalization can regenerate nonzero padding, so mask after each convolution-normalization-activation stage before the next temporal convolution, after residual addition, and after final normalization where applicable. For pre-normalization blocks, mask after normalization/activation before convolution. Channel-only normalization permits masking after the complete pointwise stage; masking every intermediate operation is unnecessary. Retain corrected baseline semantics rather than adding unrelated normalization changes. Causality and zero-padding semantics are separate requirements.

Stochastic behavior: retain inherited dropout placement. For the primary comparison, replay the same realized branch-local dropout masks across original and short evaluations of a block, while keeping masks appropriately independent across distinct dropout sites and training examples. Use explicit mask reuse or a tested branch-local RNG replay helper that handles the relevant CPU/CUDA RNG state and advances the global stream as one branch evaluation would. Record this policy. Different dilation outputs remain different despite shared masks. If reliable mask coupling cannot be implemented, declare independent branch dropout as a different specification and use it consistently across static and contextual conditions; do not claim equal-dilation equivalence or baseline stochastic equivalence. Calling the same Dropout module twice normally draws different masks.

Redundancy: a branch can be collapsed only when its full dilation schedule, inputs, shared parameters, normalization behavior and realized stochastic operations coincide. Under the primary shared-mask policy, identical schedules permit one evaluation and omission of the redundant gate. Identical dilation alone is insufficient with independent dropout. Averaging independent dropout realizations changes training noise; equality of expected outputs does not imply equality after downstream nonlinearities or losses.

Interpretation: a short-dilation branch consumes contextualized h and can still carry information from distant interactions. Identity shortcuts preserve representations but do not themselves move information across time. Neither gate values nor unit dilation establish forgetting, a bounded raw-history horizon, or an optimal temporal scale. Structural reachability should be derived from the actual convolutional graph, including both branches and residual paths; span alone can obscure gaps in reachable offsets. Older-prefix perturbations with recent activity held fixed measure retained sensitivity, not causal user preferences.

Primary controls: retain the corrected original-only baseline and prioritize a learned context-independent scalar alpha per block, initialized at zero logits, against the contextual gate with identical branch construction and initial mixing. This static control tests whether input dependence adds value beyond a globally learned scale preference. It has fewer gate parameters, so it is not a complete capacity control. If affordable, specify an active context-free residual bottleneck with approximately matched parameter count before training; unused parameters do not control capacity. Fixed 50:50 mixing, short-only, other fixed coefficients, and moderate or strongly biased initialization are explanatory follow-ups rather than a mandatory exhaustive sweep. Comparisons of initializations must match initial mixing across static and contextual gates. Do not quietly tune fixed coefficients more or less extensively than contextual variants.

Training and cost: retain the inherited objective, negative sampling and optimizer for the initial experiment. Match shared initialization and sampler draws across controls where feasible, using a dedicated reproducible sampler RNG independent of extra branch/dropout consumption and stable category identifiers rather than Python's randomized hash. Disclose unavoidable stochastic differences. All controls are separate trials with independently trained models; never fuse their outputs, inspect other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Two branch evaluations increase convolution work and retained activations despite few additional parameters. Measure host-accounted runtime and memory before committing long runs, and count checks, diagnostics, failures and controls against the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Do not promise a number of trials without runtime evidence or silently lower prescribed batch counts to accommodate the architecture.

Protocol: retain preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 logical batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and the supplied checkpoint cadence. Respect the host SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 despite its family-agnostic name. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Preserve splits and host evaluator. Select only through the arithmetic mean of four host validation HR@10 values, with 200 users per category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Preserve evaluator tie handling. No hidden test access, extra datasets or pretrained weights are permitted.

Inference and checkpoints: the predictor writer must embed the identical shared-weight architecture, gate summary width, causal padding, normalization, masking and saved configuration. Save actual architecture and initialization metadata, although loading uses trained gate values rather than reinitializing them. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint. At evaluation, dropout is disabled, and the same branch and gate formulas apply. Read the maximum nonpadding positional index for left-padded histories, never count-1; retain the supplied empty-history convention. Preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), all host ModelView interfaces, and view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. No independently fitted scorer, expert, checkpoint average or score fusion is introduced.

Diagnosis adapter: retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return measured metrics and explicit metric_definitions; the interpreter prompt must use both. The public loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B x L. Preserve fixed diagnostic negatives, valid-position masking and existing margin definitions. For gate probes, use nonpadding positions from fixed diagnostic batches in eval mode and report per-block alpha mean, variation across positions/examples, and fractions below 0.05 or above 0.95. Separate position variation from comparisons of matched positions across examples. Report normalized branch difference ||short-original||/(||short||+||original||+1e-8), branch cosine where both norms are nonzero, and zero-norm counts. During training, record actual gate gradient norms before clipping and the corresponding training step; eval-only probes cannot supply training gradient measurements. Similarity and gradient observations are descriptive, not proof that gates are useful. Existing average embedding cosine cannot establish dimensional collapse; stronger training margins alone cannot establish validation or user benefit.

Checks before long training: verify causal future-perturbation invariance, padding-stage behavior, all-padding handling, corresponding parameter identity across branches, gradients reaching shared convolutions and gate projections on deliberately distinct nondegenerate branches, and generated-predictor score agreement. Verify fixed alpha values reproduce the corresponding branch interpolation and check the analytic gate derivative on a tiny deterministic example. With dropout disabled or masks coupled, verify identical branch schedules give identical outputs; separately verify the declared dropout replay policy. Test left-padded short histories and terminal readout. These are proposed host-accounted checks, not completed results, and cannot substitute for validation.

Overfitting and shortcut learning: the controller can become static, memorize common prefixes, exploit item popularity or last-item associations, or change optimization without improving recent-purpose discrimination. Its current-state input h already contains historical information; its recent summary does not force recency-based decisions. Examine training/validation divergence, gate variation conditional on available history length and training frequency, and supported older-prefix perturbations without fitting an auxiliary recommendation scorer. Do not infer personalization from gate variability alone. Repeated configuration and checkpoint selection can overfit the fixed validation set; record every attempted configuration and retain the inherited checkpoint schedule.

Evidence and qualitative follow-up: use only public histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions. Ratings, review text, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unavailable despite generic upstream schemas. Use the prescribed twenty real training users, five per category, for full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Track specific recent-purpose matches, broad-association displacement, older-interest displacement, duplicate functionality, unsupported compatibility, unestablished project need and indeterminate identity judgments separately. Gating cannot establish compatibility or unmet demand from missing evidence. User-alignment scores express mechanistic plausibility, not measured behavioral improvement.

Reporting: report category and macro sampled-candidate HR@10 rather than claiming full-catalog gains. If the host already exposes paired user-hit indicators, report gained/lost hits and descriptive category-stratified paired bootstrap intervals without changing the evaluator. One changed hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 percentage points. Such intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates, omit training-seed/candidate-redraw variation, and do not correct repeated validation selection. If indicators are unavailable, state that paired uncertainty is unavailable. Krichene and Rendle show why sampled and exact metrics can rank models differently; the prescribed full-catalog qualitative observations are complementary evidence, not a replacement evaluation metric.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']

# Integrate into the supplied corrected NextItNet scaffold.
# All branch operations below preserve its actual order and parameterization.
# Each corresponding convolution/norm Parameter is shared across branch calls.

def causal_conv(x_BCL, weight, bias, dilation):
    k = weight.shape[-1]
    return F.conv1d(
        F.pad(x_BCL, ((k - 1) * dilation, 0)),
        weight, bias, stride=1, padding=0, dilation=dilation)

class SharedDilationBlock:
    def forward(self, h, recent_summary, valid):
        # Primary policy: same realized dropout masks at corresponding sites.
        # This helper must be implemented and checked for the inherited branch.
        original, short = paired_branch_evaluations_with_shared_masks(
            self.complete_residual_branch,
            h=h,
            valid=valid,
            original_dilations=self.inherited_dilations,
            short_dilations=tuple(1 for d in self.inherited_dilations))

        # complete_residual_branch uses functional causal dilation, tokenwise
        # normalization and masking before each temporal convolution and after
        # each pointwise stage that precedes another temporal convolution.
        if self.control == 'original_only':
            update = original
        elif self.control == 'fixed_half':
            update = 0.5 * original + 0.5 * short
        else:
            if self.control == 'learned_static':
                alpha = sigmoid(self.scalar_logit)  # one scalar/block; init 0
            elif self.control == 'contextual':
                alpha = sigmoid(self.scalar_gate(concat(h, recent_summary)))
                # Linear(2*hidden_width, 1); initialize weight=bias=0.
            update = (1 - alpha) * original + alpha * short
        return inherited_shortcut_add_and_mask(h, update, valid)

# Original-only should use its ordinary single branch, without extra computation.
# Identical schedules can use one evaluation only when full branch behavior,
# including realized stochastic operations, is identical.

def log2feats(sequence):
    valid = sequence != 0
    embeddings = item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
    recent = causal_masked_mean(embeddings, valid, width=5)
    h = inherited_input_processing(sequence)
    for block in blocks:
        h = block(h, recent, valid)
    return inherited_output_processing_with_padding_mask(h, valid)

# Primary architectural comparison: learned_static versus contextual.
# The corrected original-only baseline remains the reference.
# These are separate budgeted trials; their predictions are never combined.
for category in FOUR_INHERITED_CATEGORY_ROUTES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    sampler = inherited_sampler_with_recorded_independent_rng(...)
    model = corrected_nextitnet_with_shared_dilation_blocks(inherited_config)
    for epoch in range(min(inherited_configured_epochs, 200)):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            batch = sampler.sample_batch(...)
            inherited_training_step(model, batch)
            # At predefined steps, record measured pre-clipping gate gradients.
        inherited_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(
        category, model, complete_architecture_config,
        gate_initialization=0.0, summary_width=5,
        branch_dropout_policy='shared_realized_masks')

write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_four_category_routing()
# model.eval(); gather max index with sequence[index] != 0, never count-1.
# Preserve inherited empty-history convention; load one checkpoint/category.
# Retain ModelView and DiagnosisProbe(view, device).
# run_full_diagnosis(loader) returns measured metrics and metric_definitions.
# diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw) includes metrics and their definitions.
# Verify causality, masking, branch sharing/dropout policy and predictor agreement.
# Host selection: unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10.
# No independent scorers, averaging, fusion, hidden-test access or extra data.

originality.positive: The precise combination of corresponding shared kernels across dilation schedules and a causal recent-context scalar controller remains a specific testable synthesis within NextItNet.
originality.negative: Selective Kernel Networks, SkipRec, AdaMCT and adaptive-dilation work establish close precedents for multiscale selection and contextual computation; the earlier score of 4 overstated broad architectural novelty.

future_potential.positive: Matched static and contextual gates can clarify whether input-dependent temporal transformations add value beyond global scale preference, informing subsequent context-selection research.
future_potential.negative: The mechanism may learn static mixing or optimization shortcuts, cannot exclude distant information, and has no demonstrated benefit for current-purpose judgments or full-catalog retrieval.

code_difficulty.positive: It adds small projections, reuses convolution parameters and requires neither extra datasets nor independent prediction components.
code_difficulty.negative: The earlier score of 5 understated paired stochastic execution, masking inside residual branches, functional dilation, dual-forward cost, reproducible controls, diagnostic instrumentation and generated-predictor consistency.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes the residual causal dilated-convolution family retained by the proposed experiment.
Already models multiple temporal scales through stacked fixed dilations, constraining claims that multiscale history modeling itself is new.
limitations: Does not establish gains from the proposed shared-parameter adaptive interpolation.
The supplied corrected host implementation remains the experimental starting point.

related_work.title: Official NextItNet residual-block implementation
contributions: Provides a reference two-convolution residual branch using channel normalization and dilations d and 2d.
Clarifies that distinct convolutions within a block have distinct weights; proposed sharing occurs across corresponding dilation-path evaluations.
limitations: The TensorFlow reference does not replace inspection of the supplied corrected PyTorch implementation by the host.
Causal convolution alone does not specify complete zero-padding semantics after biased and affine operations.

related_work.title: Selective Kernel Networks
contributions: Provides a close precedent for input-dependent selection among receptive-field branches.
For two branches, softmax selection can be expressed as a sigmoid of a logit difference.
limitations: Spatially pooled context requires past-only adaptation for aligned sequential supervision.
Its branches and channelwise selection do not directly validate shared-kernel scalar gating in NextItNet.

related_work.title: SkipRec
contributions: Provides recommendation-specific precedent for sequence-dependent layer selection, including NextItNet backbones.
limitations: Layer skipping differs from soft interpolation between shared-parameter dilation transformations.
It weakens broad contextual-selection novelty claims without establishing effectiveness of this experiment.

related_work.title: AdaMCT
contributions: Uses personalized layer-specific scalar coefficients to fuse CNN and Transformer features.
The supplied search summary reports an adaptive-versus-fixed fusion comparison across three Amazon datasets, motivating fixed-mixture controls.
limitations: Local/global module fusion differs from shared-kernel dilation selection.
The cited comparison does not establish superiority over globally learned static mixing in this experiment.
Sampled-candidate evaluation does not establish full-catalog ranking improvements.

related_work.title: Highway Networks
contributions: Establishes gated interpolation between transformed and identity features.
Motivates examining initialization and gradient flow rather than treating gate bias as incidental.
limitations: Negative biases encouraging identity propagation do not establish the best initialization between two transformed convolution branches.
Saturation and branch similarity independently reduce the proposed gate's gradient.

related_work.title: WaveNet
contributions: Provides precedent for causal dilated convolutions and multiplicative feature gating.
limitations: Its tanh-sigmoid feature gate is not an interpolation between receptive-field branches.
It does not establish adaptive-scale recommendation gains.

related_work.title: Language Modeling with Gated Convolutional Networks
contributions: Introduces gated linear units with a linear content path, informing distinctions among gating mechanisms.
limitations: Feature modulation is different from scalar dilation-path selection.
Language-modeling evidence does not validate this benchmark hypothesis.

related_work.title: FADC: Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution
contributions: The supplied search results describe adapting dilation to local frequency content, providing adjacent precedent for content-dependent receptive fields.
limitations: Vision evidence does not establish recommendation gains or causal, padding-safe NextItNet behavior.
The proposed scalar interpolation does not reproduce FADC.

related_work.title: HGNCDSR
contributions: The supplied search results describe feature and instance gates for representing current interests alongside longer-term patterns.
limitations: Does not establish that residual gating removes older information.
Its setting and architecture do not establish effectiveness on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: The supplied search results describe uniform-negative warm-up and curriculum-controlled sampling hardness across sequential backbones.
limitations: Supports a separate sampling direction rather than validating the selected gate.
Combining sampling changes with the initial architectural experiment would weaken attribution.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can change model comparisons relative to exact metrics.
limitations: Does not invalidate the prescribed host benchmark, which remains the selection criterion.
Does not provide full-catalog conclusions from the available sampled validation results.

related_work.title: PyTorch LayerNorm documentation
contributions: Specifies normalized dimensions and affine parameters, supporting channel-only per-timestep normalization.
limitations: Correct causal dimensions and padding restoration remain implementation responsibilities.

related_work.title: PyTorch Dropout documentation
contributions: Documents stochastic masking during training and identity behavior during evaluation.
limitations: Repeated calls through the same module do not automatically share realized masks.
The paired-branch mask policy requires explicit implementation and verification.
